text:
lara: Heads up — `pip install redwood-python` fails inside minimal alpine/docker images because there is no wheel on PyPI. pip falls back to building sdist and I get `ERROR: Could not build wheels for redwood-python` (python3.11, pip 23.2). Any ideas?
dev-bot: publish-log: release v0.7.2 only uploaded sdist (tar.gz), no .whl found :eyes:
samir: Can you paste the pip output? Usually that means build-time deps (PEP 517) are missing in the isolated build env.
lara: Quick paste: `ERROR: Failed building wheel for redwood-python
ERROR: Could not build wheels for redwood-python, which is required to install pyproject-based projects`
kevin: Workarounds: `python -m pip install --upgrade pip build setuptools wheel` then `pip install redwood-python`, or `pip install --no-use-pep517 redwood-python` if you control the environment. But real fix = publish wheels (manylinux/mac/win) so pip doesn't need to compile.
ryan: FYI I also hit a separate issue after install — mypy complains because `py.typed` is missing. Users installing from wheel still get untyped package. We should ship types (or stubs) and include `py.typed` in wheel.
samir: I'll add a quick CI patch: run `python -m build -w` and add cibuildwheel for manylinux so release publishes wheels. Also update MANIFEST / pyproject to include `py.typed`. Opening PR now.
lara: Also a poetry edge-case: `poetry add redwood-python` resolved to the tarball and attempted to build in the venv; poets' resolver plus lockfiles can pin older build deps and fail. Recommend documenting `poetry add --no-root` or upgrading poetry, but publishing wheels avoids this.
kevin: For the typing-extensions / dependency conflict some examples had `typing-extensions==3.x` pinned in the example lockfile which collides with newer python versions. Suggest we relax to `>=4.0` in our extras and update example lockfiles.
samir: PR opened: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/429 — adds wheel builds (cibuildwheel), includes `py.typed`, updates packaging metadata, and adds a short note in RELEASE.md about publishing wheels. :white_check_mark:
lara: Tested locally after the PR build artifacts were uploaded to our test index — `python -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install --upgrade pip && .venv/bin/pip install --index-url https://test.pypi.example/simple redwood-python==0.7.3` installs via wheel and works for me :tada:
ryan: I'll update the onboarding sample-app README to call out: `pip install --upgrade pip build wheel` and link the PR. Also add a note for poetry users recommending `poetry self update` and to prefer the wheel release.
kevin: Follow-ups: 1) add CI step that uploads wheels to PyPI on tag releases 2) bump docs and example locks 3) ensure extra `async` feature is declared in `pyproject` so `redwood-python[async]` resolves cleanly.
lara: Thanks all — ping me when PR merges and I'll close the GH issue.
